chunks: I asked him about what the people relate: that a sealed parchment was entrusted to Umm Salamah. So he said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed away, ʿAlī (عليه السلام) inherited his knowledge, his weapons, and what was there. Then it passed to al-Hasan, then it passed to al-Husayn (عليه السلام). Then, when we feared that we would be overcome, he entrusted it to Umm Salamah. Then, after that, ʿAlī ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام) took possession of it.
He said: So I said, Yes, then it passed to your father, then came to you, and after that it came to you? He said: Yes.

key_terms.أُمِّ سَلَمَةَ: Umm Salamah, to whom the entrusted item was given for safekeeping
key_terms.سِلَاحَهُ: his weapons, symbolizing transmitted authority and inheritance
key_terms.صَحِيفَةٌ مَخْتُومَةٌ: a sealed parchment containing entrusted material
key_terms.عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ: Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Husayn عليه السلام, who later received it
key_terms.عِلْمَهُ: his knowledge, inherited from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: How were the Prophet’s صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم knowledge and weapons transmitted among the Imams عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the transmission of the Prophet’s صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم knowledge, weapons, and entrusted items through the line of the Imams عليهم السلام. It also mentions their temporary entrusting to Umm Salamah during a time of danger, affirming the continuity of divinely designated authority and inheritance within the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Hujr, from Humran, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about what the people narrating that a sealed Parchment had been handed over to Umm Salma<sup>as</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When (the soul of) Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was Captured, Ali<sup>asws</sup> inherited his<sup>saww</sup> Knowledge, and his<sup>saww</sup> weapons, and whatever was there. Then these came to be to Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>. Then these came to be to Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>. So when we<sup>asws</sup> feared losing them (in the plunder at Kerbala), these were entrusted to Umm Salma<sup>as</sup>. Then Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> took possession of these after that’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I said, ‘Yes, then these came to be to your<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>, then ended up to you<sup>asws</sup>, and they came to be to you after that?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya from ibn Muskan from Hujr from Humran who has said the following. “ I asked abu Ja‘far (a.s.) about the truth in the matter which people relate that a sealed page (or pages) was given to ’Umm Salama.” The Imam (a.s.) then said, “When the Messenger of Allah passed away, Ali (a.s.) inherited his (Holy Prophet’s ) arms and whatever was therein, then it was transferred to Imam al-Hassan then to Imam al-Husayn (a.s.). However, then we became anxious about loosing them we then decided to leave them in trust of ’Umm Salama. Afterwards Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) took custody of the arms.”
I then said, “Then it is true that it was transferred to your father and then they ended up to you.”
